entries_new.name: Beijing Economic and Technological Development Zone
entries_new.founder: Approved by China's State Council (catalogue section for State Council-approved zones)
entries_new.story:
Beijing Economic and Technological Development Zone (北京经济技术开发区) is a national-level development zone in Beijing, China. China's 2018 audit catalogue of development zones, published by the National Development and Reform Commission and five other ministries, lists it among zones approved by the State Council, as a national economic and technological development zone, approved in August 1994, with an approved area of 3980 hectares (code G111001).
Zones of this kind give firms tax, customs or administrative concessions while Chinese law still applies.

sources.t: China development zone audit catalogue (2018 edition), NDRC announcement 2018 No. 4
Catalogue attachment (PDF), National Development and Reform Commission
Special economic zones of China, Wikipedia

entries_new.founder: Approved by China's State Council (catalogue section for State Council-approved zones)
entries_new.story:
Haimen Economic and Technological Development Zone (海门经济技术开发区) is a national-level development zone in Jiangsu province, China. China's 2018 audit catalogue of development zones, published by the National Development and Reform Commission and five other ministries, lists it among zones approved by the State Council, as a national economic and technological development zone, approved in January 2013, with an approved area of 488 hectares (code G321099).
Zones of this kind give firms tax, customs or administrative concessions while Chinese law still applies.

sources.t: China development zone audit catalogue (2018 edition), NDRC announcement 2018 No. 4
Catalogue attachment (PDF), National Development and Reform Commission
Special economic zones of China, Wikipedia

entries_new.founder: Approved by China's State Council (catalogue section for State Council-approved zones)
entries_new.story:
Yantai Economic and Technological Development Zone (烟台经济技术开发区) is a national-level development zone in Shandong province, China. China's 2018 audit catalogue of development zones, published by the National Development and Reform Commission and five other ministries, lists it among zones approved by the State Council, as a national economic and technological development zone, approved in October 1984, with an approved area of 1000 hectares (code G371029).
Zones of this kind give firms tax, customs or administrative concessions while Chinese law still applies.

sources.t: China development zone audit catalogue (2018 edition), NDRC announcement 2018 No. 4
Catalogue attachment (PDF), National Development and Reform Commission
Special economic zones of China, Wikipedia

Hebei Xinji Economic Development Zone (河北辛集经济开发区) is a provincial-level development zone in Hebei province, China. China's 2018 audit catalogue of development zones, published by the National Development and Reform Commission and five other ministries, lists it among zones approved by provincial governments, approved in August 2006, with an approved area of 484.18 hectares (code S137001).
Zones of this kind give firms tax, customs or administrative concessions while Chinese law still applies.

entries_new.story:
Jiangxi Leping Industrial Park (江西乐平工业园区) is a provincial-level development zone in Jiangxi province, China. China's 2018 audit catalogue of development zones, published by the National Development and Reform Commission and five other ministries, lists it among zones approved by provincial governments, approved in March 2006, with an approved area of 321.37 hectares (code S369020).
Zones of this kind give firms tax, customs or administrative concessions while Chinese law still applies.

sources.t: China development zone audit catalogue (2018 edition), NDRC announcement 2018 No. 4
Catalogue attachment (PDF), National Development and Reform Commission

Lushan County Industrial Cluster Zone (鲁山县产业集聚区) is a provincial-level development zone in Henan province, China. Zones of this kind give firms tax, customs or administrative concessions while Chinese law still applies.

entries_new.founder: Approved by the Sichuan provincial-level government (catalogue section for provincially approved zones)
entries_new.story:
Sichuan Beichuan Economic Development Zone (四川北川经济开发区) is a provincial-level development zone in Sichuan province, China. China's 2018 audit catalogue of development zones, published by the National Development and Reform Commission and five other ministries, lists it among zones approved by provincial governments, approved in June 2012, with an approved area of 355.36 hectares (code S517068).
Zones of this kind give firms tax, customs or administrative concessions while Chinese law still applies.

sources.t: China development zone audit catalogue (2018 edition), NDRC announcement 2018 No. 4
Catalogue attachment (PDF), National Development and Reform Commission

entries_new.name: China (Shanghai) Pilot Free Trade Zone
aka: 中国（上海）自由贸易试验区
entries_new.founder: State Council of China
entries_new.story:
China (Shanghai) Pilot Free Trade Zone (中国（上海）自由贸易试验区) is one of the 22 pilot free trade zones China has set up since 2013; China Daily, a state newspaper, dates this one to 2013. China Daily describes these zones as special economic areas with a set boundary, where reforms in investment, finance, trade and government functions are tested so they can be copied elsewhere. The Shanghai zone was the first, opened on 29 September 2013, and China Daily says China's first negative list for foreign investment (a list of sectors closed or limited to foreign investors) followed it. A Lingang New Area was added to it in 2019.
Zones of this kind give firms tax, customs or administrative concessions while Chinese law still applies.

sources.t: 每日一词 | 自由贸易试验区 pilot free trade zones (China Daily, 24 April 2025)

aka: 中国（海南）自由贸易试验区
entries_new.founder: State Council of China
entries_new.story:
China (Hainan) Pilot Free Trade Zone (中国（海南）自由贸易试验区) is one of the 22 pilot free trade zones China has set up since 2013; China Daily, a state newspaper, dates this one to 2018. China Daily describes these zones as special economic areas with a set boundary, where reforms in investment, finance, trade and government functions are tested so they can be copied elsewhere.
Zones of this kind give firms tax, customs or administrative concessions while Chinese law still applies.

sources.t: 每日一词 | 自由贸易试验区 pilot free trade zones (China Daily, 24 April 2025)
